cells.tense: Present — you're here, and you can see it.
cells.verb: beginning to see clearly, before there's anything to do about it
cells.place: in the part of you that knows what it's actually drawn toward
cells.ask: Let the seeing go one step further than you can use yet — look at the next thing without asking what it means for you. What comes back is light you don't have to prove: you're clear because you are, not because you argued for it.
cells.core: You can see what you actually want. Not the whole route, not the timeline — just the direction, in focus, for the first time in a while. Nothing has to be done with it yet. The clarity is doing its work just by being there, and you're not reaching to make it more than it is.
cells.sheetLine: You can see where you're pulled, and you're letting it be that simple.

cells.tense: Future — you're squinting at a distance that hasn't arrived.
cells.verb: seeing ahead of anything to see
cells.place: in the part of you that knows what it's actually drawn toward
cells.ask: Pick one thing you already see and carry it through today as it stands, without checking the distance for a truer version. Fresh eyes on the ordinary morning, not the far one. What comes back is a light that holds because it's yours, not because you kept proving it to yourself.
cells.core: You're scanning for the real pull, and the scanning has gotten ahead of the pull. Every flicker gets held up and examined for whether it's the one — and the moment anything clears, you're already looking past it for a clearer one. The seeing was supposed to show you a direction. It's turned into watching for one.
cells.sheetLine: You're looking so hard for the real pull you can't rest in any of them.

cells.tense: Past — you're steering by a sighting you took a long time ago.
cells.verb: no longer looking up to see
cells.place: in the part of you that knows what it's actually drawn toward
cells.ask: Don't try to see harder. Finish one small thing on purpose — chosen, carried to the end, because you meant it. Deciding from the ground up pulls the looking-up back with it. What comes back is light you don't have to strain for: clear because you are, not because you forced it.
cells.core: You stopped looking. There was a direction once — you saw it, you set out — and you're still walking by that first glimpse, not by anything you've seen since. The pull may have moved. You wouldn't know; the eyes that would catch it have been down for a while, and the walking kept going anyway.
cells.sheetLine: You're following an old glimpse and not taking a new look.

cells.tense: Disowned present — you've already seen it and you're calling it nothing.
cells.verb: already seeing clearly, and not saying so
cells.place: in the part of you that knows what it's actually drawn toward
cells.ask: Before you do anything about it, say "I see it" about one thing you've been calling a passing mood. Just the seeing, stripped of what it would cost. What comes back is light you can stand in without defending — clear because you are, not because you made a case.
cells.core: You know which way you're pulled. It's clear every time the subject comes up — a lean, a quiet yes, a flinch at the other options — and you file it as a passing thought, a mood, nothing to steer by. The seeing already happened. You're just not signing your name to it.
cells.sheetLine: You already see which way you're pulled. You're calling it a mood.
